- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model tends to lag; anticipate reversal and adjust downward slightly.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with weighted average of recent 7–14 days.
- If true outcome diverges sharply from model in first 5–7 days (e.g., sudden spike or drop), model is lagging; apply early correction based on sentiment direction.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative phase, model often misses the momentum; forecast should accelerate slightly in next 3–5 days.
